input: Get the car's brakes inspected this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is just an inspection or if suspected repair/replacement is also expected changes what kind of appointment to book and how long to allow.
Whether the user has a preferred mechanic or dealership already in mind determines if they need to research providers or simply call a known one.
Understanding what prompted this — a noise, a warning light, routine maintenance — affects the urgency and what to tell the mechanic.
A budget ceiling affects whether to go to a dealership, independent shop, or chain — and whether to pre-authorise any repair work found.
Knowing whether the user needs alternative transport while the car is in the shop (ride, loaner car) is a critical next-action dependency.
Clarifying what 'done well' means — a written report, a pass/fail verdict, a cost estimate — shapes what to ask the shop to provide.
The user's preferred day or time window within the month affects when to schedule and how much lead time is needed to secure a slot.

gold.taskTitle: Get car brakes inspected this month
gold.taskDescription: Arrange and complete a brake inspection for the user's car within the current month.

questions.title: Is this inspection only, or do you expect repairs too?
questions.description: Determine whether the goal is purely a diagnostic inspection or if the user anticipates brake repairs or part replacements as part of this visit.

questions.title: Do you have a mechanic or shop already in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a trusted provider to call, or if they need help identifying and vetting a brake specialist.

questions.title: What prompted you to get the brakes checked now?
questions.description: Understand the trigger — unusual noise, spongy pedal, warning light, or routine mileage interval — to gauge urgency and inform the mechanic accurately.

questions.title: Is there a budget limit for this visit?
questions.description: Establish a spending ceiling so the user can choose the right type of shop and decide in advance whether to authorise any repair work discovered.

questions.title: Will you need alternative transport while the car is in?
questions.description: Determine if the user needs to arrange a loaner car, ride-share, or other transport on the day of the inspection, as this affects scheduling.

questions.title: What do you want the shop to give you at the end?
questions.description: Clarify the expected output — a written inspection report, a verbal pass/fail, a repair cost estimate — so the user knows what to request when booking.

questions.title: Which days or times this month work best for you?
questions.description: Pin down the user's available windows so the appointment can be booked with enough lead time to secure a suitable slot before month end.
